title: Two letters, three characters
hook: How long is "a" followed by a smiley, and are two ways of writing "e with acute" equal?
concept: Text has several layers: bytes, code units, code points and what a person sees. Languages count different layers by default. Equal-looking text can also be stored as different sequences, so a plain comparison fails.

checks.label: Length of "a" plus one emoji (what a user sees: 2)
Is the single character é equal to e plus a combining accent?

worlds.js: length counts UTF-16 code units, so the emoji counts as 2 and the total is 3. Spreading the string iterates code points. The two accent spellings compare unequal until normalized.
worlds.python: len counts code points, so the length is 2 and correct. The accent spellings are still unequal until you call unicodedata.normalize.
worlds.java: length() counts UTF-16 code units and returns 3. codePointCount gives 2. Normalizer handles the accent comparison.

fix: Count the unit your users care about (code points at minimum, graphemes for real user-facing limits) and normalize text before comparing or hashing it.

regression.python:
import unicodedata

assert unicodedata.normalize("NFC", "\u00e9") == unicodedata.normalize("NFC", "e\u0301")
assert len("a\U0001F600") == 2
